_target: Odoo 19 only (the workbook describes the v19 AvaTax surface; the v15 OCA fork has different fields and methods)
_policy: AUTOMATION_CONVENTIONS rule 4 says a test whose essence needs an external system must be a blocked stub. Twelve of these fourteen cases ARE the Avalara call, so a literal reading would leave FG-05 permanently unverified. Approved deviation: the cases run for real against the Avalara SANDBOX ONLY, behind tests/fg05/common.py::require_sandbox, which BLOCKS unless the company has Use AvaTax on, avalara_environment == 'sandbox', and both credentials readable as set. A production-pointed company is always BLOCKED, never run.

TC-DAT-017.reason: Setup verification, read-only. Fully offline except workbook step 3 (Test connection), which is gated on the same sandbox conditions and reported as NOT EVALUATED rather than blocking the other seven steps. Adaptation: the workbook compares against a Novobi printout the platform does not hold, so the test asserts every structural invariant that does not need it and logs the full captured inventory (fiscal positions + both AvaTax account codes, category mappings, partner exemptions, company flags) as a CSV artifact for the human tick-off.

TC-TAX-001.reason: Full flow against the sandbox: draft invoice 1,000.00 x 1, Compute Taxes (button_external_tax_calculation), totals block, Avalara Code, Confirm. Posted invoice is left in place per the workbook's State After The Test.

TC-TAX-002.reason: GATE 3 for the whole feature group. Reads the journal entry, not the invoice: asserts more than one tax line, that the tax lines sum exactly to amount_tax, and that every tax name carries the bracketed authority code the MMG override preserves (a name without it is a FAIL).

TC-TAX-003.reason: Counts account.tax records for the authority code before and after a second invoice to the same address, including archived rows so an archived namesake cannot mask a duplicate.

TC-TAX-007.reason: The only FG-05 case that needs no Avalara credentials, so it is deliberately NOT behind require_sandbox and can be run while waiting for the sandbox. The ship-to address guard is pure server-side Python (mmg_account_avatax_enhancement._check_partner_shipping_address via @api.constrains), so it fires on save; the test handles both the save-time and compute-time timings. The two Compute Taxes presses that would reach Avalara are individually sandbox-gated.

TC-TAX-008.reason: Quotation tax preview, 2,000.00 x 1: non-zero Taxes, Total == Untaxed + Taxes, Avalara Code present, no error.

TC-TAX-009.reason: Two-address comparison on one quotation (Phoenix AZ vs Missoula MT). Builds its own quotation instead of continuing TC-TAX-008's, because the platform forbids depending on another test's fixtures.

TC-TAX-010.reason: Order-to-invoice carry-over, all three figures compared to the cent. Builds the starting state the workbook chain hands over (Missoula MT, 2,000.00 x 1). The invoice's own Avalara Code is asserted non-empty and deliberately NOT asserted equal to the order's, because the workbook says a difference is correct.

TC-TAX-011.reason: Partially provable in Odoo. Asserted here: Commit Transactions is on (BLOCKED if not), the posted invoice has a non-empty Avalara Code and non-zero tax, and a computed-but-unposted invoice stays draft with commit False. RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP, printed into the execution log with both codes and both figures: sign in to the Avalara SANDBOX portal and confirm the posted document is present and committed and that Avalara's total tax matches. The platform cannot reach the portal.

TC-TAX-013.reason: Exempt customer vs a taxable control customer in the same state, both at 1,000.00. The control is a real assertion, not a log line, because a zero on both means AvaTax is not calculating at all. BLOCKED (not FAILED) when the company has no usable avatax.exemption; the workbook's own remedy (Sync Parameters) is named in the reason but never executed, since it writes records and calls Avalara.

TC-TAX-014.reason: Adaptation: the workbook mutates a LIVE product category and its own If-It-Fails column warns that leaving a test code on one mis-taxes everything in it. The test creates an FG05 product category and switches that instead, which proves the same behaviour with none of the risk, and still captures/restores/asserts the original value in a finally block.

TC-TAX-015.reason: Invoice tax line on the Avatax Invoice Account, credit-note tax line on the Avatax Refund Account, amounts equal in absolute value (signs differ between out_invoice and out_refund). BLOCKED when the fiscal position has only one account or the two are the same, pointing at TC-DAT-017 as the owner of that setup gap. Builds and posts its own source invoice.

TC-TAX-016.reason: Mixed taxable (1,000.00) and exempt (500.00) lines. The 'tax on the taxable line only' expectation is proved against a control invoice containing just the taxable line, rather than by a ratio.

TC-TAX-017.reason: Deliberate break-and-restore of the API KEY, the highest-risk case in FG-05. Safety: the key's readability is probed BEFORE any write and the test BLOCKS if it cannot be read back (an unrestorable key must never be overwritten); it also BLOCKS if the key already reads as the invalid string, which means an earlier run did not restore. The restore flag is armed before the write, so a timeout after the server commits still triggers the restore. The restore runs in a finally block and is asserted by SHA-256 fingerprint, so a failed restore is a visible FAILED check. No credential value ever reaches a log, an assertion or an artifact.
